title: Cleaning Messy Data with pristineR
text: Data cleaning one common repetitive tasks data analysis workflows. Real-world datasets often contain inconsistent date formats, messy column names, missing values require lot tedious cleaning analysis can begin. pristineR package provides functions simplify common data-cleaning tasks safer user-friendly workflows. vignette demonstrates use: clean_names(), safe_date_parse(), quick_summary() using included messy_survey dataset.
code: library(pristineR)

title: Cleaning Messy Data with pristineR
text: package includes example dataset called messy_survey. dataset intentionally contains inconsistent column names, mixed date formats, missing values.
code: messy_survey #>    Student.Name Exam.Score. Submission.Date #> 1     Alex Jenk          95      2024-01-01 #> 2   Bob Johnson          88      01/02/2024 #> 3 Charles Swift          NA    March 5 2024 #> 4    Daisy Slim          76      2024/04/10 #> 5      Eve Trop          91      05-15-2024

title: Cleaning Messy Data with pristineR
text: Messy column names can make analysis difficult. clean_names() function converts names standardized snake_case formatting.
code: cleaned_data <- clean_names(messy_survey)  names(cleaned_data) #> [1] "student_name"    "exam_score"      "submission_date"

title: Cleaning Messy Data with pristineR
text: Datasets often contain dates stored multiple formats. safe_date_parse() function safely converts dates standard Date objects.
code: cleaned_data$submission_date <-   safe_date_parse(cleaned_data$submission_date)  cleaned_data #>    student_name exam_score submission_date #> 1     Alex Jenk         95      2024-01-01 #> 2   Bob Johnson         88      2024-01-02 #> 3 Charles Swift         NA      2024-03-05 #> 4    Daisy Slim         76      2024-04-10 #> 5      Eve Trop         91      2024-05-15

title: Cleaning Messy Data with pristineR
text: quick_summary() function generates common summary statistics numeric variables. summary includes: mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, missing value counts.
code: quick_summary(   cleaned_data,   c("exam_score") ) #> # A tibble: 1 × 6 #>   variable    mean    sd   min   max missing_n #>   <chr>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <int> #> 1 exam_score  87.5  8.19    76    95         1

title: Cleaning Messy Data with pristineR
text: following example demonstrates complete cleaning workflow using pristineR.
code: cleaned_data <- messy_survey |>   clean_names()  cleaned_data$submission_date <-   safe_date_parse(cleaned_data$submission_date)  summary_table <- quick_summary(   cleaned_data,   c("exam_score") )  summary_table #> # A tibble: 1 × 6 #>   variable    mean    sd   min   max missing_n #>   <chr>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <int> #> 1 exam_score  87.5  8.19    76    95         1
